Aideation · Piloted at the University of Montana

CSCI 391 · Agentic Artificial Intelligence

Design, build, and operate AI agents that reason, plan, use tools, remember, and know when to stop.

  • LevelIntermediate · Upper-division undergraduate
  • Length15 weeks · 2 sessions per week
  • Includes14 modules · 22 narrated tracks · 5 labs · 2 projects
  • PrerequisiteData Structures & Algorithms (CSCI 232) or instructor consent
  • CostFree and open
Go to the course →
Download the course mapThe whole course on one board · PDF

What you'll learn

  • Explain the core concepts behind agentic AI systems and large language models
  • Decide when an agent is justified — and when a workflow, classifier, or single LLM call is better
  • Design agents that use external tools and APIs through explicit, versioned schemas
  • Build memory-enabled and retrieval-augmented (RAG) agents with deliberate write and recall policies
  • Apply planning, single-agent, and multi-agent architecture patterns, including MCP
AI agentsTool useAgent memoryPlanningMCPMulti-agent systemsHuman oversightEvaluationGuardrails

14 modules

  1. What Is an AI Agent?
  2. The Minimum Viable Agent & a Short History of Agents
  3. The Anatomy of an Agent
  4. When Not to Build an Agent
  5. LLMs as Reasoning Engines & Tools as Contracts
  6. Memory: Working, Episodic, Semantic, Procedural
  7. Planning & Decomposition
  8. Model Context Protocol (MCP)
  9. Single-Agent Patterns
  10. Multi-Agent Systems & Shared Infrastructure
  11. Human-in-the-Loop & Human-on-the-Loop
  12. Long-Running & Asynchronous Agents
  13. Observability, Evaluation & Drift
  14. Safety, Alignment & Guardrails
